record.title: GUI burst open treats failed container-side collection as success (empty baseline or no burst) with no audit record
record.description: When the first agent GUI input of a burst arrives, AgentBox._snapshot takes a docker-commit snapshot and then calls _open_gui_burst. That method collects the /workspace manifest and the desktop process baseline. Two silent fail-open paths exist. (a) Exit status unchecked (observed live): SandboxManager.workspace_manifest runs the root `find ... | head -c` exec and returns `_parse_manifest(res.output[0] or b"")` without checking res.exit_code. If the in-container command cannot run, it returns ({}, False) with no exception, and _open_gui_burst records the burst against an empty baseline. desktop_processes and kill_processes ignore exec status in the same way. At close, the diff reports every pre-existing file as added. The audit event carries counts and truncated=True plus only the first 100 sorted paths, so the real GUI-made change can fall outside the listed paths, and nothing records that the baseline collection failed. Parent-live l7 measured this on agentbox-desktop:0.1 with the pids cgroup at 1022-1024/1024, using pressure created by direct docker exec as uid 1001: the manifest had 0 entries, the burst was recorded, the audit showed only tool_request/policy_decision/snapshot/tool_result, and a close after the pressure ended gave gui_changes added=301, truncated=True, with the real change zz_changed_by_gui.txt absent from the listed 100. (b) Exception swallowed: if either collector raises, the bare `except Exception: return` at service.py:210 records no burst. Later GUI inputs inside the idle/interval window open no new burst, so there is no stray kill and no gui_changes for that window. The same pattern at :221 and :238 skips the kill or the diff at close. A mock reproduces this, but no agent-reachable raising trigger is known. Agent reachability (parent-live l9): an approval-free exec under the default read-only-exec rule (uid 1000) filled the pids cgroup to 1024/1024 within about 1 s, and a concurrent agent GUI input (key shift) still returned 200 and recorded a burst with 0 manifest entries and no audit marker. The pressure did not release itself: the exec ended with exit 254, about 1000 uid-1000 processes survived, pids stayed at 1022/1024 even after a root `pkill -x tail` by the parent, and a close under that pressure logged no gui_changes at all. A sandbox wedged this way can start no new processes, which limits what the agent can do while the condition holds. Not yet shown: an agent-only sequence that ends with a misleading or absent gui_changes record while a real GUI-made change exists. Bounds: the burst snapshot is still taken and logged, so the restore point survives. gui_changes is a detective, partial control, and the GUI is approval-free by design (N-1). Provenance: the l7/l9 scripts imported the working branch /home/user/agentbox rather than the audited tree. The burst, collector and policy code they exercise is byte-identical between the two, so the results apply to the audited source. The decisive live runs are the parent's.
record.claimed_root_cause: Burst bookkeeping treats a failed container-side collection as a successful one. workspace_manifest (sandbox.py:495-501), desktop_processes (sandbox.py:689-692) and kill_processes (sandbox.py:697) never check exec exit status, and _open_gui_burst/_stop_gui_strays/_close_gui_burst (service.py:210, 221, 238) swallow every exception. In both cases there is no audit event and no fail-closed fallback, such as refusing further GUI input or marking the burst baseline invalid.

trace.description: Agent token (lowest-trust principal, own sandbox) sends a GUI input tool (key/click/type). Policy default is allow, with no approval.
On an allowed GUI input that starts a burst (_gui_needs_snapshot true), it calls _snapshot.
After docker commit, it opens the GUI burst with the new snapshot id.
Root find exec result is parsed without checking exit_code. A failed exec returns ({}, False) instead of raising.

Burst is recorded with the empty manifest as its baseline, with no audit event marking the collection as failed. A later gui_changes diff reports all existing files as added and can leave the real change out of the 100 listed paths.

evidence.description: except Exception: return in _open_gui_burst. A raising collector leaves no burst and no audit record.
except Exception: return in _stop_gui_strays. A failed ps/xdotool/kill skips the stray kill silently.
except Exception: return in _close_gui_burst. A failed close-time manifest skips gui_changes silently.
gui_changes lists only v[:100] of each sorted diff list plus counts and a truncated flag, so an empty baseline buries the real change.
desktop_processes ignores the ps exit status. A failed exec yields an empty process list.
kill_processes ignores the kill exec's exit status.
read-only-exec allow rule includes tail, so the l9 pressure exec is approval-free.
Live: under pid pressure, workspace_manifest returned 0 entries with no exception.
Live: first GUI input still 200, burst recorded with baseline manifest entries 0.
Live: after pressure ends, the next GUI input opens no new burst, so the degraded burst persists.
Live: close gives gui_changes added=301, truncated=True, and the real change is not in the listed 100 paths. Control at line 3 shows added=1 with the change listed.
Live: the agent's approval-free exec drove pids to 1024/1024 within about 1 s, before the GUI input.
Live: the agent's GUI input under that pressure returned 200 and recorded a burst with 0 manifest entries.
Live: the audit shows only tool_request, policy_decision, snapshot and tool_result, with no event marking the failed collection.
Live: the agent exec ended with exit 254 while pids stayed at 1022/1024, so the pressure is not self-releasing.
Live: with the pressure persisting, the close logged no gui_changes record, so the end-to-end misleading-diff result via the agent-only path is not shown.
Live: after the exec returned, about 1002 uid-1000 processes remained in state S.
The script imports the working branch, but the burst/collector/policy code it exercises is byte-identical to the audited tree.
Mock: a raising workspace_manifest at open leaves no burst, with no new burst on the next input, no kill and no gui_changes (lines 3-5).
Real SandboxManager collectors with a fake container whose exec exits 126 return empty results without raising.
Real _close_gui_burst with an empty baseline: added=301, truncated=True, real change not listed. The control on line 15 lists it.
Default policy decides allow (read-only-exec) for the pressure command.

blockers: Not observed on the live image: an agent-only sequence that ends with a misleading or absent gui_changes record while a real GUI-made change exists. l9 shows only the first half (agent exec pressure, then agent GUI input, then an empty-baseline burst with no audit marker). The pressure did not release (exit 254, pids stayed at 1022/1024, even after the parent's pkill), so the change step and close ran under full pids and the close logged nothing. Decisive missing facts: (a) whether the pressure can be released, or left with enough headroom for the open to fail while later steps still work; (b) whether a GUI-made change that needs no new process is recorded or silently missed at close. This needs a parent-live Docker observation; the verifiers have no Docker access.

No agent-reachable trigger is identified for the exception path at service.py:210/221/238 (a Docker API error, a container not running, or the docker client's read timeout during collection). This path stays mock-only.

validation_plan.local: Parent-live, Docker-backed, disposable desktop sandbox, dummy tokens, scratch AGENTBOX_HOME, loopback only, importing the audited tree. Create 300 workspace files, then reproduce the l9 empty-baseline burst. Restore headroom (record whether an agent-reachable means sufficed or the host had to release it), make a GUI-only change to /workspace/zz_changed_by_gui.txt, wait past gui_snapshot_idle, and read GET /audit as the human. The finding holds if the burst has 0 manifest entries, no event marks the collection failure, and gui_changes shows added about 301, truncated=True, with the change unlisted. The control without pressure must show added=1 with the file listed. Also check the persistent-pressure case: a change made with a shell builtin in an already-open terminal, and whether the close leaves any record. The finding is refuted if the GUI input fails with 503 or the manifest is complete. Fix check: the collectors raise SandboxError on a nonzero exit, and the burst methods log a gui_burst_error audit event and mark the baseline invalid.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a non-production desktop sandbox with the deployment's pids, exec timeout and GUI idle settings: confirm whether the human-facing timeline shows any sign that the burst baseline was lost, whether the pressure persists after the exec returns, and whether the GUI-made change is visible without restoring the burst snapshot.
